note: Found on 2026-10-02. A Schlumberger sounding reading 21.1 ohm-m almost everywhere, with three misreads. Both engines converge to two layers of 20.6 and 22.2 ohm-m at the same misfit (9.53687 percent, equal to 5e-7) with the boundary at 0.8316 m in Python and 0.8304 m in the browser, 1.4e-3 apart where parity holds a model to 1e-3. The Python inversion puts that boundary's thickness uncertainty at a factor of 10, and the report already calls it poorly resolved: the data do not say where it is to better than tenfold.
open: Should parity hold the two engines to 1e-3 on a parameter the toolkit itself reports as uncertain by a factor of 2 or more? The fuzz suite's inversion generator leaves such boundaries out of its comparison (see compare() in fuzz_parity.py); this case stays here, held to diverging, until that is decided one way or the other.
